nodes.title: Story Creator
widgets_values: A little fox who wants to see the northern lights

WORLD: A snowy northern land in winter, soft blue and pink light, cozy and magical. Pip is a small orange fox with big curious eyes, a fluffy white-tipped tail and a knitted blue scarf; there is only one Pip. Only the characters that a scene names are in the picture.
[wide, slow push-in] Evening inside a cozy den dug under a snowy hill, warm firelight on round earth walls: Pip, a small orange fox in a knitted blue scarf, sits on a rug by a small crackling fire next to Grandpa, an old grey fox with a white muzzle and a wooden walking stick || In a den under a snowy hill lived a little fox named Pip.
[medium shot] Inside the cozy den by the fire: Pip, the small orange fox in the knitted blue scarf, jumps up and points excitedly at an old painting on the wall that shows green and purple lights over a mountain, his tail wagging || Pip: Grandpa, are the northern lights real?
[close-up, slow push-in] Inside the cozy den, firelight on his face: Grandpa, the old grey fox with a white muzzle, leans on his wooden walking stick and smiles warmly, then nods slowly || Grandpa: They are real. They dance above the tallest mountain.
[close-up on their paws] Inside the cozy den by the fire: Grandpa, the old grey fox, places a small round wooden compass with a glowing green needle into the open paws of Pip, the small orange fox in the blue scarf || Grandpa: Take this. The needle always points to the lights.
[continue] [wide shot] Morning outside the round wooden door of the den under the snowy hill: Pip, the small orange fox in the knitted blue scarf, waves goodbye with one paw and holds the compass in the other || So the next morning, Pip set off with the compass.
3D animated family movie, soft warm lighting, rich colors, detailed fur
Pip, a small orange fox with big curious eyes, a fluffy white-tipped tail and a knitted blue scarf
A warm, calm storyteller voice narrates

Upbeat indie pop with warm female vocals, bright electric guitars, punchy drums, melodic bass, and subtle synth layers. Catchy and energetic, with an uplifting summer atmosphere, a memorable chorus, and polished modern production.

[Verse]
Morning light across the window
City waking down below
I can hear the streets are calling
Feels like somewhere we should go

[Chorus]
Run with me into the sunlight
Leave the shadows far behind
We don't need to know tomorrow
Tonight the whole world feels alive

nodes.title: How to use
widgets_values:
## How to use - tested on RTX 3060 12 GB

**What it does:** you give it a script, it makes the whole story video: the same character in every scene, every scene moving, characters that talk on screen, a narrator, music. Like the 'long AI story video' trend, but on your own PC.

**Best results: let a big chatbot write the script.** Paste the structure prompt from the README (HOW TO WRITE A SCRIPT) into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini with your story idea and paste its answer into **Script**. The small built-in writer (**Write the scenes for me**, the 8B Qwen text encoder) is still in here but off: it writes short, vague lines and forgets how side characters look.

1. **Script** - one line per scene. The parts of a line (these tags are like little embeddings the workflow reads):
   - `WORLD: ...` (first line, optional) - the look of the whole story, put in front of every scene. Without it the 8B writer makes one from your scenes.
   - `[camera]` at the start - wide shot, close-up, tracking shot, slow push-in, low angle... it goes into the picture and the video prompt, so the video model moves the camera.
   - `what we see` - write the place, every character with their full look (only your hero has a picture), the objects, and the action from start to end. More detail = more movement and the right things in frame.
   - `|| Name: what they say` - that character says it on screen (mouth moves). Keep it to about 12 words.
   - `|| what the narrator says` - a line without a name is the narrator: the scene is made without voices, the narrator line is made in its own small pass with one narrator voice for the whole story and laid on top.
   - `[continue]` at the start - transition: this scene's clip ends on the next scene's picture (first and last frame) instead of a cut. Use it only where the action really flows on; cuts are the default.
2. **Style** goes in front of every scene; **Character** describes your hero. Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo makes one character picture, then every scene still as an edit of it, so it stays the same character. Or switch on **Use my own character picture** and un-bypass the loader (select + Ctrl+B).
3. Scene length is automatic: 3-9 s, from how much is said in the line.
4. MiniMax H3 (8-step turbo LoRA) turns each still into a clip with its sound; YuE2 makes the song (Music style + lyrics), each scene gets its slice of it at **Music volume (dB)**.
5. **Upscale to 1080p** (on): every scene is scaled to 1920x1080 before it's saved.
6. Every scene is saved as it finishes (`story/scene_...`), its voice on its own (`story/stems/voice_...`), then the story (`story/story_...`).

| Story (0.4 MP) | Scenes | RTX 3060 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 min (v1.0, turbo LoRA) | 12 | 43:38 |
| 5 min (v1.2, FastH3, no upscale) | 58 | 3:35:26 |
| 5 min (v1.4 script, FastH3, no upscale, two runs of 29) | 58 | ? |

Most of the time is H3. RAM: ComfyUI's memory grows about 0.6 GB per scene on a 32 GB PC; for more than about 30 scenes run the script in two halves and join them in your editor.

**Tips (from the tests)**
- Name every character with their full look in every line they're in - unnamed or half-described side characters turn into copies of your hero.
- Avoid over-the-shoulder shots and characters cut off at the frame edge: the hero appears twice or two characters melt together.
- Write what happens, not what it means: 'the needle swings and settles on the left path' instead of 'Pip decides'.
- About two thirds dialogue, one third narrator makes the story feel alive.

Double-click the node to see every step. **Colours inside the node:** 🟦 load models · 🟩 your input (pose, face, frames) · 🟪 prompt + conditioning · 🟧 sampling · 🟨 decode + video · ⬛ settings + switches · 🟦‍ cyan = extras (side by side)

nodes.title: Base prompt + your idea
widgets_values:
Write a short animated story as exactly {n} scenes, one scene per line, nothing else.
Format of every line:  what we see || what we hear
- "what we see": one sentence describing the picture: who is there, what they do, where.
- "what we hear": the narrator's sentence, OR a character speaking as  Name: words  (for example  Pip: Look at the stars!).
- About one line in four is a character speaking, the rest is the narrator. At most 12 words after the ||.
- Describe every character fully every time they appear (species, colors, clothes), they must look the same in every scene.
- The story has a beginning, a problem, and a happy ending in the last scene.
- No numbering, no titles, no blank lines, no extra text before or after. No quotation marks.
- EVERY line has || in it, also the lines where a character speaks: the speaking goes after the ||.
Example of two lines:
A small orange fox in a blue scarf sits on a snowy hill at dusk || High in the snowy north lived a little fox named Pip.
The orange fox looks up at an old grey owl on a pine branch || Pip: Hello, Mister Owl!
Story idea: {i}

widgets_values:

Write ONE short paragraph of at most 90 words, no list, no title: where and when the story happens (the place, the season,
the light and the colors), then EVERY character that appears in the story by name, each with how they look (species, size,
colors, clothes) in a few words. Do not describe what the main character is doing.
Only things that stay the same in every scene. No story events.
